Auto off deactivates an active file that nobody has used for 30 minutes (the default). It is on for every file unless an editor turns it off.

File In use while Robot System Someone has the Station open in a browser tab, or an AI agent or a Project VPN tool works with the Station Robot World Someone watches it in Theater

Running nodes and a playing World do not count as use: a World left playing with no viewer is deactivated like an idle one.

When nobody is using an active file, a yellow countdown appears under its state: Auto off in N min. It stops when somebody opens the file, and starts a minute or two after the last person leaves.

docs.title: Turn Auto Off Off
docs.text:
To keep a file active on purpose, clear its Auto off box. The portal warns that the file is billed for every minute it stays active: click Turn off and keep billing to confirm, or Keep it on.

The warning before Auto off is turned off

The file then stays active, and keeps using credits, until somebody deactivates it. Tick the box to turn Auto off on again.

Deactivate what you no longer need. Auto off is a safety net, not a replacement for deactivating.

docs.title: 6. Messages and Errors
docs.text: Message What to do Activating and deactivating needs edit access to this project. Your role is Can view. Ask a manager for Can edit. Another Robot World is already running in this project Deactivate the active World first. This workspace has run out of credits. … See When Credits Run Out. The … plan runs at most N Systems and Worlds at once. … Deactivate another Robot System or Robot World first; stopping it is not enough. Environment failed to activate Read the reason under it, then choose Active to try again.

docs.title: Robot Systems and Robot Worlds
docs.text:
A project holds two kinds of file: Robot Systems, which run robot software in Stellar Station, and Robot Worlds, which simulate the place where the robots work.

File What it is Edit it in Work with it live in Robot System One Stellar Station ("the Station"): its node graph, documents, settings and apps Station · Edit Station · Live Robot World A simulated environment: a scene with your robots, the ground and lighting Studio Theater

Design documents, such as gateway documents (.gw) and robot documents (.sdd, .sddm, .sdda), are not project files: they live inside a Station or in a library.

docs.title: 1. Create a File
docs.text:
1. In the project, click New file. An empty project also offers Create new file.
  2. Choose Robot System or Robot World and click Next.
  3. Enter a File Name (up to 20 characters) and, if you like, a Description (up to 40 characters).
  4. For a Robot System, choose its Starting apps.
  5. Click Create. The new file appears in its table, Inactive.

docs.title: Starting Apps
docs.text:
Starting apps offers bundles of Store apps for the new Station: Empty (No apps; install what you need from the Store.), Manipulator, Mobile robot and Legged (MMC). The apps install when the Station first starts. If some apps could not be added, the portal names them: install them from the Station's Store (Apps and Packages).

A new Robot World has no scene yet. Open it with Studio to build one (Studio); until then it has nothing to run.

docs.title: 2. Import an .sdr File
docs.text:
A Sodero file (.sdr) holds one Robot System or one Robot World. Importing it creates a new file in the project, with the name and description stored in the .sdr.

  1. In the project, click Import. An empty project also offers Import file.
  2. Choose the source: From your PC (drag the file onto the dialog, or click Choose file), My Library or Project Library.
  3. Click Import.
Importing an .sdr file from your PC

The new file appears under Robot Systems or Robot Worlds, depending on what the .sdr holds.

docs.title: Move Robot Systems Between Stellar X and Sodero Cloud
docs.text:
Check compatibility before transfer

The .sdr extension does not guarantee that every Station version accepts the same graph and document formats. Check the destination release and its installed apps (Compatibility).

For compatible Station releases, export and import Robot Systems with Export SDR and Load SDR on Stellar X, and Download local copy and Import in Sodero Cloud. Consult the destination product’s instructions before proceeding:

  • From Stellar X: export the Station on the controller with Export SDR, then import the file into a project.
  • To Stellar X: download a local copy of the Robot System, then load it on the controller with Load SDR.

Check apps and packages after a move. An .sdr does not contain installed packages. After importing one from Stellar X, install the apps its nodes need. Before loading one on Stellar X, install the packages the Station uses on the controller.

A Robot World's .sdr opens in Sodero Cloud only.

docs.title: 3. File Actions
docs.text:
The ⋯ button at the end of a file's row opens its menu.

The menu of a Robot System, as a manager sees it Item Shown to Does Copy link Everyone Copies the project's link; a file has no page of its own Add to favorites Everyone Lists the file under Favorites on Home Duplicate file Editors and managers Copies the file in the same project, for example jackal copy. A Station copy keeps its documents and apps. File details Everyone The file's information. Editors and managers can change its name, description and icon color here. Download local copy Managers Saves the file as an .sdr (Download a Local Copy) Move to trash Editors and managers Moves the file to Trash after you confirm. An active file is deactivated first, and a Station saves its data on the way down.

An official Sodero World cannot be duplicated. A World that uses official Sodero files is copied without them: add those assets to the copy again in Studio. To bring back a trashed file, restore it from Trash (Move to Trash, Restore and Delete).

docs.title: 4. How Robot Worlds and Robot Systems Work Together
docs.text:
The Robot Systems of a project drive the robots in the project's active Robot World. You do not enter any address.

  • One active World per project. A project can hold several Robot Worlds, but while one is active, the others cannot be activated (Another Robot World is already running in this project).
  • Active Stations connect automatically to the project's active World, including their camera and IMU gateways. A Station activated before the World connects once the World is up.
  • Robots are matched by name. A simulation gateway drives the robot named in its gateway document (Robot name): the name of the robot's articulation prim in the World, for example jackal. Use one gateway per independently controlled robot or joint group, and avoid overlapping actuator ranges.
  • Projects stay apart. A Station never reaches a World in another project. Keep the World and the Robot Systems that drive it in the same project.

Step by step: Drive Robots in the World.

docs.title: Libraries
docs.text:
Libraries hold the files you reuse across Robot Systems and Robot Worlds: .sdr files, documents, scenes and other assets.

Library Holds Who sees it Who adds and deletes files My Library Your personal files of any type Only you You A project's library Files shared with one project Everyone with access to the project The workspace's owner and admins, and members when Members can manage the Library is on Sodero Assets Official robots, environments and documents from Sodero Everyone Nobody: it is read-only

The Library window lists the project libraries under Workspace Library, while some dialogs call the open project's library Project Library. Both names mean the project's library.

docs.title: 1. Open the Library
docs.text:
Click Library in the left navigation bar. The Library window has two tabs:

  • My Library: your personal files.
  • Workspace Library: the libraries of the workspace's projects. Click a project to see its files; the back arrow returns to the list of projects.

Both tabs have a search box, a type filter, a sort button and Add file. Each file has an Export button, which saves a copy on your computer, and a Delete button.

docs.title: 2. Add Files
docs.text:
1. In My Library, or in a project under Workspace Library, click Add file.
  2. Choose the source:
    • From your computer: drag a file onto the dialog, or click Choose file.
    • In My Library, Workspace Library: copy a file from a project library you can open.
    • In a project's library, My Library: copy a file from your personal library.
  3. Click Add file.
The library of Warehouse Demo under Workspace Library

A file can be up to 2 GiB.

docs.title: 3. Use Library Files
docs.text: File Where you use it .sdr Import on the project page creates a Robot System or Robot World from it (Import an .sdr File) Gateway and robot documents (.gw, .sdd, .sddm, .sdda), camera settings, map bundles In the Station, when you load a document into a node (Documents and Settings) Scenes and assets (.usd, .usda, .usdc) In Studio, to build a World (Studio)

docs.title: 4. Delete Library Files
docs.text:
Click the file's Delete button. In a project's library, it is shown only to the people who may manage libraries.

Deleting a library file removes it at once; it does not go to Trash. Export a copy first if you may need the file again.

docs.title: 5. Sodero Assets
docs.text:
Sodero Assets is the official content that Sodero publishes for everyone: robots, grounds, lighting and sky images for Studio, and robot and gateway documents for Manipulator, Mobile and Legged robots in the Station.

Sodero Assets are read-only, and you can view, edit and simulate them only in Sodero. A World that uses them keeps them in Sodero: its local copy and its duplicates leave them out. An official Sodero World cannot be downloaded or duplicated.

docs.title: 6. Storage Limits
docs.text: Your workspace's plan limits how much the libraries can hold. Billing & Usage shows the Project libraries, Your My Library and Workspace storage meters (Credits and Usage). A file that does not fit is refused with a message that names the limit: delete files you no longer need, or contact Sodero.

docs.title: Projects
docs.text: A project holds the Robot Systems and Robot Worlds that belong together and decides who can open them. Every project belongs to a workspace.

docs.title: 1. The Project List
docs.text:
Click Projects in the left navigation bar. The portal also opens here after you sign in.

The project list of Acme Robotics

Each row shows the project's name and description, its Contents (for example 1 System · 1 World), its Members, My access (your role) and Last modified. A star marks a favorite, and a green Running badge shows while a file of the project is active.

Click a project to open it. The ⋯ button at the end of a row opens the project menu:

Item Shown to Does Manage access Managers Invites people, changes roles and sets the project access (Share and Collaborate) Add to favorites Everyone Lists the project under Favorites on Home Duplicate project Managers Copies the project Project settings Managers Name, description and project information Move to trash Managers Moves the project to Trash

docs.title: 2. Create a Project
docs.text:
1. On the project list, click + Project. A workspace without projects also offers Create new project.
  2. Enter a Name (up to 20 characters) and, if you like, a Description (up to 40 characters).
  3. Choose the Project access: Restricted (Invited people only, the default) or Workspace (All members of this workspace).
  4. Click Create. The new project opens.
The Create project dialog
  • If + Project is dimmed, only the workspace's owner and admins can create projects there. The owner can turn on Members can create projects (Workspaces and People).
  • Your workspace's plan limits how many projects the workspace can hold; projects in Trash do not count (Credits and Usage).

docs.title: 3. The Project Page
docs.text:
Click a project on the list to open it. The top bar shows Projects (back to the list), the project's name and your access.

Warehouse Demo, with the Robot System jackal and the Robot World warehouse Control Does Project VPN Connects your computer to the project's Stations (Project VPN) AI agents Shows how to connect an AI agent, and the project link to give it (AI Agents) Search files, Filters Show only the files whose name contains a text, or of one type or state Import Creates a file from an .sdr file (Import an .sdr File) New file Creates a Robot System or a Robot World (Create a File)

Editors and managers also see the selection bar under the toolbar (0 selected · Worlds: 0/1, Clear, Actions), which handles several files at once.

The files are listed in two tables, Robot Systems and Robot Worlds. Each row shows the file's Activation and Running state, the Actions links that open it, a Station's IP address, Auto off, Active users, Resource use and Last modified (Activate and Run). Clicking a row selects the file; files open only from their Actions links. The ⋯ button at the end of a row holds the file actions.

docs.title: 4. Project Access and Roles
docs.text:
Project access decides who can open the project: only the people invited to it (Restricted, the default), or also every member of the workspace (Workspace). Managers change it in Manage access (Share and Collaborate).

Each person in a project has one of three roles, shown in lists as Manager, Editor and Viewer:

  • Can manage, for people who look after the project: access, copies, downloads and Trash.
  • Can edit, for people who build and run the Robot Systems and Robot Worlds.
  • Can view, for people who look and review without changing anything.

The person who created a project can manage it, and so can the workspace's owner and admins.

Action Can view Can edit Can manage Open the project; see its files, their states and active users ✓ ✓ ✓ Open Station · Edit, Station · Live, Studio and Theater view only ✓ ✓ Create, import, duplicate, rename and trash files — ✓ ✓ Activate, run, stop and deactivate files; change Auto off — ✓ ✓ Download a local copy of a file — — ✓ Invite people, change roles, set the project access — — ✓ Duplicate the project, change its settings, move it to Trash — — ✓ Restore or permanently delete the project's items in Trash — — ✓

Controls you cannot use are dimmed and give the reason on hover. Creating projects, managing project libraries and Empty all trash depend on your workspace role.

docs.title: Rename or Describe a Project
docs.text: Open the project's ⋯ menu, choose Project settings, change Project Name (up to 20 characters) or Description, and click Save.

docs.title: Duplicate a Project
docs.text:
Choose ⋯ › Duplicate project. The copy, for example Warehouse Demo copy, is created in the same workspace, with the same description and project access.

  • Every Robot System and Robot World is copied with its files. Each Station copy keeps its documents and its apps.
  • Official Sodero Worlds, and the official Sodero files that other Worlds use, are left out. A message names them.
  • Check Manage access on the copy and invite the people who need it.
  • The copy counts toward your plan's project limit.

docs.title: 6. Download a Local Copy
docs.text:
Managers can keep a Robot System or Robot World outside Sodero: open the file's ⋯ menu on the project page and choose Download local copy. The browser saves an .sdr file named after the file, for example jackal.sdr. To keep a whole project, download each of its files.

Use the copy to keep a backup, to import it into another project, or to load a Robot System on a Stellar X controller with Load SDR (Backup and Restore in the Stellar X manual).

Tip: A Station saves its data when it deactivates. Deactivate the Robot System before you download it, so that the copy holds your latest changes.

Official Sodero content stays in Sodero. An official Sodero World cannot be downloaded, and a World that uses official Sodero files is downloaded without them.

docs.title: 7. Move to Trash, Restore and Delete
docs.text:
To move a project to Trash, open its ⋯ menu on the project list, choose Move to trash and confirm. Its active files are deactivated first, which ends their use of credits.

Click Trash in the left navigation bar to see the trashed projects, Robot Systems and Robot Worlds. The ⋯ menu of an entry, shown to the people who can manage it, offers:

  • Restore, which puts it back. Restoring a project needs room under your plan's project limit.
  • Delete permanently, which removes it for good. This cannot be undone.

Workspace owners and admins also have Empty all trash: after asking, it permanently deletes every entry they can manage.

Library files do not go to Trash. Deleting a file from My Library or from a project's library removes it at once (Libraries).

docs.title: Share and Collaborate
docs.text: Work on a project with other people: invite them with a role, send them the project link and see who is working where. Sharing is set per project; membership of the workspace itself is covered in Workspaces and People.

docs.title: 1. Invite People
docs.text:
Managers invite people from the project list:

  1. Open the project's ⋯ menu and choose Manage access.
  2. Under Invite people, type an email address, or pick one of the workspace members it suggests.
  3. Choose the role: Can manage, Can edit (the default) or Can view (Project Access and Roles).
  4. Click Invite. The invitation goes out at once.
The Manage access dialog

The person receives an email titled Sodero project access: Warehouse Demo with a Review access button. The invitation is valid for 7 days; inviting the same address again replaces it. If the dialog says Couldn't send invitation. Try again., check the address: the person may already have access.

docs.title: Change Roles, Remove People, Set the Access
docs.text:
People with access lists everyone in the project with their role.

  • To change a role, use the person's role menu. To remove someone, click X.
  • Project access at the top of the dialog switches between Restricted and Workspace.
  • Click Save to apply these changes. Cancel drops them; invitations already sent stay.

You cannot change your own role, and a project always keeps at least one manager.

docs.title: 2. Accept an Invitation
docs.text: The invited person clicks Review access in the email, signs in with the address the invitation was sent to and clicks Accept invitation. To decline, they ignore the email. Details and messages: Accept an Invitation.

docs.title: 3. Guests
docs.text: People invited to a project without being members of its workspace join it as guests. They find the project in the workspace menu under Switch workspace › Guest projects (N) (Guest Projects). Inside the project, a guest has the role they were invited with, like anyone else.

docs.title: 4. Send the Project Link
docs.text:
Every project has a link that opens it in the portal. Copy it with Manage access › Copy link, with a file's ⋯ › Copy link, with AI agents › Copy project link, or from the browser's address bar.

The link opens the project only for people who are signed in and have access to it, so invite new people first. The same applies to the link icon next to an active file's Station · Live or Theater link, which copies the address of that live view.

docs.title: 5. See Who Is Working
docs.text:
The Active users column of the project page shows who is working in each file right now. Click the avatars for each person's name, role and activity:

Activity The person is Station Design Editing the Station in Station · Edit Station open Working in Station · Live Recent Station API activity Using the Station through an AI agent or the Project VPN Theater viewer Watching the World in Theater Studio collaboration Editing the World in Studio

For recent activity in the whole workspace, such as projects created or files started and stopped, see Notifications.

docs.title: 6. Work Together on One Station or World
docs.text:
Several people can work in the same file at the same time:

  • Station. Everyone who opens a Robot System works on the same Station.
  • Studio. Everyone who opens a World in Studio joins the same editing session (Studio).
  • Theater. Everyone who opens an active World watches the same simulation, each in their own rendering mode. Each RTX Real-time viewer has its own cloud renderer, which uses credits.

People with Can view can look but not change anything. For example, Go live is disabled for them in Station · Edit.

Tip: Agree on who activates, runs, stops and deactivates a shared file. These actions change the file for everyone working in it.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: Sodero Cloud and Stellar X share robot-system concepts and document types. Their deployed Station versions, installed apps and operator interfaces can differ.

docs.title: Before You Configure a Robot
docs.text:
1. Check that the required app is available in the current Station's Store and can be installed for this environment.
  2. Use gateway and robot documents exported for that Station version. An app listing or an upload confirmation alone does not confirm that the controller is ready to operate.
  3. After going live, check the selected documents, port connections and node states before issuing motion commands.
  4. Open an operator UI only when the running app provides its link or Open … action. If unavailable, stop here and contact Sodero for supported packages and instructions.

The controller chapters describe their functions when these prerequisites are met. The Quick Start covers World creation and viewing; it does not require a controller UI.

docs.title: Move Files Between Products
docs.text:
An .sdr is a transfer container, not a guarantee of compatibility with every Station release. Check document format, node names, required apps and destination architecture before importing. Installed packages are not included in the file.

A Robot World's .sdr is for Sodero Cloud. For a Robot System, follow Import an .sdr File and the destination product's documentation. Keep the original backup until the imported system has been checked.

Cloud instructions use Store, Station · Edit, Go live and Station · Live. A Stellar X manual for an earlier device release may use different menus and node names. Use it for the concepts and device-specific steps that match your installed version; do not copy old graph identifiers into Cloud unchanged.

docs.title: Example Scene and Robot Documents
docs.text:
The Quick Start includes a warehouse scene and its accompanying license notice. A scene alone does not configure its robot controller.

Obtain compatible .gw, .sdd, .sddm or .sdda documents from the current product's supported asset collection or from Sodero. Keep required metadata and license notices intact. Do not edit an archive's internal files to force acceptance by a different Station version.

docs.title: Browser and Rendering
docs.text: Use an up-to-date supported browser. WebGPU requires browser, operating-system and GPU support; a browser version number alone does not guarantee availability. RTX Real-time renders in the cloud and needs a working streaming connection. Check the rendering choices available on your device.

docs.title: External Tools
docs.text: Install Project VPN only when the portal offers an installer for your operating system. Follow the prompts of that release. Connect AI agents using the endpoint and configuration shown in the project's AI agents panel.

docs.title: Limits and Defaults
docs.text: This page collects the fixed limits and the defaults you can meet in Sodero Cloud, each with the page that explains it. Your workspace's plan sets further limits, such as storage and how many Robot Systems and Robot Worlds can be active at once: Billing & Usage shows them (Set by Your Plan).

docs.text:
Your workspace's plan sets these limits. Billing & Usage, in the workspace menu, shows each one with what the workspace uses (Credits and Usage):

  • credits, their hourly rates and when they renew;
  • Projects in the workspace;
  • Workspace storage, Project libraries and Your My Library;
  • Systems and Worlds running at once;
  • AI agent (MCP) tool calls, Project VPN time and Project VPN data per calendar month.

Plans differ, so this manual gives no values for them. To change the plan or add credits, contact Sodero.

docs.title: Apps and Packages
docs.text:
Check the app itself in Store. A Starting apps bundle is a selection of apps, not confirmation that every required app is installed or available for the current environment. Verify the gateway and controller separately after going live.

Every node of a Station runs an app or module that is installed on that Station. Add node offers only what is installed, plus empty drafts. Apps come from the Store; your own programs are uploaded as module packages. Both are kept with the Robot System and installed each time its Station starts.

Source What it is Badge in Add node Where you install it Store app A program published by Sodero, such as the actuator gateway or a robot controller SODERO Store in the left rail Your own module A module package (.tar.gz) that you built CUSTOM Modules › Add custom module, or Package on the Live page

docs.title: 1. Starting Apps
docs.text:
When you create a Robot System, Starting apps offers bundles of Store apps, for example for a manipulator or a mobile robot. Empty has none (Create a File). The apps of the chosen bundle are recorded with the Robot System and install when the Station first starts.

If Add node lists only Empty gateway, Empty controller and the other drafts, no app is installed yet. Install the apps you need from the Store.

docs.title: 2. The Store
docs.text:
Click Store in the left rail. The Store lists the apps that Sodero publishes, one row each.

The Store of a new Robot System, on the Edit page Part of a row Shows Name The app and a short description, for example Gateway Designer (Gateway control and setup workspace) Included Every Store app is included in Sodero Cloud; there is nothing to buy State Not Installed or Installed Versions Current (the Store's release), Installed version, New when a newer release is out, and Installed (the date). An installed app also lists its Cloud permissions: what its own UI may use in Sodero Cloud, such as your libraries. Buttons Install or Uninstall, and Update when a newer release is out

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Click Install. When the app installs depends on the page:

  • Edit page: the app is recorded for the Robot System and installs when the Station starts.
  • Live page: the app installs at once and is recorded for the Station's later starts.

The app then appears in Add node, under the node type it declares, with the SODERO badge (Add a Node).

docs.title: Update
docs.text: Update (Update to …) replaces the installed release with the Store's current one. While a node of the app runs, the button is disabled (Stop its running instances to update it): stop those nodes first. On the Edit page, Update records the new release, which installs when the Station starts.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text: Uninstall removes the app from the Robot System. While a node of the app runs, the button is disabled. While the saved graph still has nodes of the app, it is refused with a message that names them: delete those nodes, then uninstall.

docs.title: The Modules Page
docs.text: Click Modules in the left rail. Used modules in this system lists the Station's modules with Name, Type, Publisher (Sodero or Custom), Version and Used by, the number of nodes that use each one. The ⋯ menu of a row offers Module info (version, publisher, source, size and the nodes that use it) and Remove module.

docs.title: Upload a Module Package
docs.text:
1. Click Add custom module.
  2. Drop one or more packages (.tar.gz or .tgz) on the dialog, or click to choose them.
  3. Click Add module (Add N modules for several).

On the Live page, Package in the toolbar does the same from the graph: choose one or more packages, and they upload one after another (Uploading 1/2 · …).

As with Store apps, a package uploaded on the Edit page installs when the Station starts, and one uploaded on the Live page installs at once. Either way it is kept with the Robot System. Your module then appears in Add node under the type it declares, with the CUSTOM badge.

How to build a module package is described in Create Custom Modules in the Stellar X manual. In Sodero Cloud:

  • Stations run on x86-64 computers. Build the native programs in your package for x86-64 (amd64).
  • Keep packages small. Every uploaded package is installed again each time the Station starts, so large packages make starting and stopping slower.

docs.title: Remove a Module
docs.text: Stop and delete the nodes that use the module, then choose ⋯ › Remove module in its row. The dialog says how many nodes still use it; click Remove to confirm.

docs.title: Documents and Settings
docs.text: Most nodes work from a document: a gateway runs a gateway document (.gw), a robot controller runs a robot document (.sdd, .sddm or .sdda). Some apps also have settings that you edit in the node's inspector. This page shows how to give a node its document, which kinds exist, and how to change settings.

docs.title: 1. Choose or Upload a Document
docs.text:
Select the node. The Parameters section of its inspector has one field for each document the app reads, for example Gateway project on an actuator gateway or document (robot) on a controller.

The inspector of a new actuator gateway: no document yet
  • The dropdown lists existing documents and may offer Built-in default (no document). For robot operation, select the document intended for that robot; do not treat an empty document field as proof that its controller is configured.
  • The line under it tells where the document came from, for example Uploaded: jackal.gw · 1 KB · …, or Not uploaded.
  • Upload brings in a new document.

docs.title: Upload a Document
docs.text:
1. Click Upload under the field. The dialog is named after the kind, for example Upload gateway-project document or Upload robot document.

  2. Choose where the file comes from:

    Tab Files From your PC Drop the file on the dialog, or click Choose file My Library Your personal library Workspace Library This project's library (Libraries) Sodero Assets Robot and gateway documents published by Sodero, under Manipulator, Mobile and Legged

  3. Click Import.

Uploading a gateway document from your PC The same dialog for a robot document

The Station confirms the upload, for example jackal.gw uploaded as the gateway-project document jackal, and the node takes the new document. If the upload fails, the message says why: … was not uploaded — ….

  • A new document is named after the last part of the node name: for sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal it is jackal (Name the Node).
  • If the field already names a document, the upload replaces that document.

Upload robot documents from the Live page. Go live first, then upload .sdd, .sddm and .sdda documents in the controller's inspector.

After the upload, reopen the node and confirm that the intended document is still selected. Upload controller documents on the Live page, while the node is stopped, before starting it.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• A running node keeps its document. Stop the node before you upload a new document for it or change its settings.
  • Each controller takes its own kind: .sdd for sodero.mmc, .sddm for sodero.mlc, .sdda for sodero.amc.
  • A robot document names its gateway and the gateway's actuators it uses. Connect the controller's servo_link to that gateway, and give the gateway at least as many actuators as the document uses.

docs.title: 2. Kinds of Documents
docs.text:
Kind File Used by Gateway document .gw Actuator gateways, sodero.actuator_gateway.<name> Robot document .sdd (manipulator), .sddm (mobile base), .sdda (articulated robot) sodero.mmc.<name>, sodero.mlc.<name>, sodero.amc.<name> Camera document .yaml Camera gateways, sodero.camera_gateway.<name> Map bundle A .nav folder packed as .tar.gz, .tgz, .tar or .zip, for example site.nav.tgz The localizer, the navigator and visual odometry

A Station has one map bundle: the localizer, the navigator and visual odometry share it, and a new upload replaces it. What a map bundle holds is described in Load and Configure a Map in the Stellar X manual.

docs.title: 3. Settings
docs.text:
Some apps declare settings. The inspector then shows one section per settings file below Parameters, titled by the app.

  1. Stop the node if it runs.
  2. Change the fields.

  3. Click Save settings (Settings saved.). Reload discards your changes.

  4. When the settings belong to a document, the section shows once the node has one: Choose or upload a … document in Parameters; its … settings then appear here.

  5. Some apps can create the file for you: click Create with defaults.
  6. The fields themselves come from each app.

docs.title: 4. Make Documents in Stellar Designer
docs.text:
Gateway and robot documents are made in Stellar Designer: the Gateway Designer makes .gw documents, and the manipulator, mobile robot and articulation editors make .sdd, .sddm and .sdda documents. Every editor and field is described in the Stellar X manual: Stellar Designer and Gateway Designer.

  • A simulation gateway's document also names the robot it drives in the World (Drive Robots in the World).
  • Ready-made documents for Sodero's robots are in Sodero Assets.

docs.title: Documents with Old Node Names
docs.text: Documents made before the node names changed to sodero.… still name nodes rc.…, for example rc.actuator_gateway.jackal. The Station refuses them: the message says that the file uses an obsolete format, or names an Obsolete robot file or an Obsolete gateway filename. Export the document again from a current Stellar Designer and upload the new file.

docs.title: 5. Messages
docs.text: Message What to do Only … files can be imported. The file has the wrong extension for this field. Check the kind in the dialog's title. … is not a robot document (expected a .sdd, .sddm or .sdda file). Export the robot from Stellar Designer as .sdd (manipulator), .sddm (mobile) or .sdda (articulation) … uses an obsolete format. … The document still uses old node names (Documents with Old Node Names) Robot '…' cannot take a new file while …, Gateway '…' is in use: … or Stop the camera before replacing its configuration A running node uses the document. Reload, then repeat your change.

docs.title: Build the Graph
docs.text: A Station is a graph of nodes connected through ports. This page shows how to add and name nodes, connect them, and keep a large graph tidy. You can change the graph on the Edit page and on the Live page; every change is saved automatically. The node types are explained in Key Concepts.

docs.title: 1. Add a Node
docs.text:
1. Click Add node in the toolbar, or right-click the empty canvas.

  2. Choose the node type: Gateway, Controller, Compound or Application.

    Choosing the node type

  3. Under Select a module, choose the app or module, then click Next.

    Gateway › sodero.actuator_gateway

  4. Enter the node name and click Add node. You can rename the node later.

    Naming the node

The node appears on the canvas as Planned. Nothing runs until you start it on the Live page (Run and Monitor).

docs.title: The Module List
docs.text:
Badge Entry Detail line SODERO An app installed from the Store Sodero package · and its version CUSTOM A module package you uploaded Imported package · Installed DRAFT Empty gateway, Empty controller, Empty compound, Empty application Empty subsystem to develop yourself (no package): a placeholder with no program behind it, for sketching a system. It does not start.

Each type lists only the apps and modules installed on this Station. To add another, install it first (Apps and Packages).

docs.title: Name the Node
docs.text:
The name field proposes the app's own name, for example sodero.actuator_gateway. Add a last part that names the robot or device, so that the name reads sodero.<package>.<name>:

Node Example name Actuator gateway of a robot sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal Mobile base controller of the same robot sodero.mlc.jackal Manipulator controller sodero.mmc.arm Articulation controller sodero.amc.dog Strider sodero.strider
  • The last part names the node's documents. A new document you upload to sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal is named jackal (Documents and Settings).
  • Robot documents refer to their gateway by its node name, for example sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal. Give the gateway the name its controller's document expects.
  • Give a robot's gateway and controller the same last part. The graph stays easy to read.
  • Names use letters, digits, _, . and -, start with a letter or digit, and have up to 60 characters (an empty draft: 20). Each name can be used once per Station: … is already a node of this graph: use another id, e.g. ….2.

docs.title: 2. Node Cards
docs.text:
Part Meaning Title The node name Second line The app or module the node runs REQUIRES n/m Ports the node needs from other nodes, on the left edge of the card: connected / total PROVIDES n/m Ports the node offers, on the right edge: ports with at least one connection / total State Planned until the node first starts, then its running state (Node States)

The card border has the color of the node type: orange for gateways, blue-violet for controllers, purple for compounds and mint for applications. The arrow at the top right of a card folds its ports away.

docs.title: 3. Connect Ports
docs.text:
Connect a port that one node requires to a matching port that another node provides:

  • Drag from one port dot to the other.
  • Click one port, then the other.
  • In the inspector of the node that requires the port, click Auto-connect next to the port. The Station connects the first matching port it finds, or shows No match.

The Station accepts a connection only when the two ports are on different nodes, one requires and the other provides, and both use the same interface. The inspector shows each port's interface under its name, for example api.actuator.servo.v1. The Station also keeps the system's structure:

  • Only a controller may use a gateway.
  • An application uses controllers or compounds, never gateways directly.
  • One controller drives a gateway.

A refused connection says why, for example Connect ports on different nodes with opposite directions and matching contracts.

To remove a connection, select the node and click Disconnect next to the port in the inspector.

Check Auto-connect with several robots. Auto-connect does not look at node names: with two gateways in the graph, it may pick the other robot's. Check the result, or drag the connection yourself.

docs.title: Common Connections
docs.text:
Node (requires) Port Connect to (provides) sodero.mmc.<name>, sodero.mlc.<name>, sodero.amc.<name> servo_link The robot's actuator gateway sodero.actuator_gateway.<name>, port servo_link sodero.strider mobile_base The mobile base controller sodero.mlc.<name>, port mobile_base sodero.strider localization The localizer, sodero.localizer sodero.strider navigation The navigator, sodero.navigator

Strider drives what its ports are connected to (Strider).

docs.title: 4. Rename and Delete
docs.text:
• Rename: click the pencil next to the node name in the inspector and enter the new name. The node keeps its connections and the documents it uses.
  • Delete: right-click the node and choose Delete node. The dialog asks Delete "…" from this robot system?; click Delete node. The node's connections are removed too.

On the Live page, stop a node before you rename or delete it.

Deleting a node cannot be undone. Everyone working on the Station sees the change at once.

docs.title: 5. Find Your Way in a Large Graph
docs.text:
• Filter shows only nodes of one Node type or Status; Reset all clears it.
  • Fit view zooms to show every node; Auto layout arranges the nodes by their connections.
  • The N issues chip at the left of the toolbar lists problems, such as Required port "servo_link" is not connected. Locate jumps to the node.

docs.title: 6. Load and Export the Graph
docs.text:
• Export downloads the graph as a .yaml file. If something runs on the Live page that the graph does not show, it asks first: Planned topology only or Also include what is running.
  • Load YAML loads such a file from your PC, My Library or the Project Library. It replaces the nodes and connections of the Station (… loaded — N nodes now in the system.).

The file holds the graph only: nodes, their parameters and their connections. Documents, settings and apps are not part of it. To copy a whole Robot System, use Duplicate file, or Download local copy and Import, on the project page (Robot Systems and Robot Worlds).

docs.title: Stellar Station
docs.text: Every Robot System is one Stellar Station ("the Station"). In the Station you build the robot system as a graph of nodes, give the nodes their documents, start them, and watch their state and logs. This manual describes the Station opened from the Sodero Cloud portal; device versions may differ.

docs.title: What a Robot System Is
docs.text:
A Robot System holds one Station and everything it needs:

Part What it is Node graph Gateways, controllers, compounds and applications, and the connections between their ports (Build the Graph) Documents and settings Gateway and robot documents, camera files, map bundles and node settings (Documents and Settings) Apps and modules The Store apps and your own module packages that the nodes run (Apps and Packages)

A Robot System drives robots in the project's active Robot World (Drive Robots in the World). You create it on the project page (Robot Systems and Robot Worlds). Nodes, ports and node types are explained in Key Concepts.

docs.title: 1. Open the Station
docs.text:
On the project page, the Robot System's Actions column holds the link:

  • Station · Edit while the Robot System is inactive. It opens the Edit page.
  • Station · Live while it is active. It opens the Live page; opening it does not start any node.

The Station opens in a new browser tab and uses your portal sign-in. The header shows the project and the Robot System, for example Warehouse Demo / jackal. People with Can view can open both pages, but every control that changes something is disabled for them (Project Access and Roles).

docs.title: Edit and Live
docs.text:
The Station has two pages for the same Robot System:

Edit page Live page Badge EDIT LIVE, with how long the Station has been live The Station Inactive: nothing runs and no credits are used Active: it uses credits (Credits and Usage) What you can do Add, connect, rename and delete nodes; set parameters; select Store apps Upload and confirm controller documents while their nodes are stopped, then start nodes, inspect logs and open available operator UIs Button Go live Stop live The Edit page of a new Robot System
  • Go live activates the Station, like Active in the portal's Activation column. A banner follows the start, and Cancel stops it. When the Station is ready, usually after about a minute, the tab moves on to the Live page by itself.
  • Stop live asks first: Every node stops and the system goes back to edit mode. Nodes and connections stay saved. It deactivates the Station, like Deactivate in the portal, and the tab returns to the Edit page.
  • When someone else activates the Station while you are on the Edit page, your tab moves on to the Live page as well.

docs.title: 2. Screen Layout
docs.text:
Area Contents Header Project and Robot System, the EDIT or LIVE badge, Go live or Stop live, Resources, and the people who have the Station open Left rail Runtime (the graph), Modules and Store (Apps and Packages); at the bottom Notifications, Help and your account Toolbar The save state (Saved), Filter, Load YAML, Export and Add node. The Live page adds Package and Start all nodes, and Adopt running when something runs that the graph does not show. The last button shows or hides the inspector. Canvas The node cards and their connections. At the bottom: zoom, Fit view, Auto layout, and folding or unfolding all cards. Inspector The selected node: name, module and state, Connection, Parameters and settings, Logs (Live page only) and Activity

The Sodero mark at the top left opens the Station menu: Back to Sodero Cloud, Libraries (My Library, Project Library), Theme (Midnight or Twilight), Help & Feedback and About Stellar Station.

Tip: Right-click the empty canvas to add a node, and right-click a node for its actions.

docs.title: 3. What Is Saved Where
docs.text:
What Where it is kept Changes to the graph Saved automatically on both pages. The toolbar shows Saving…, then Saved; if a save fails, it shows Retry save. Changes made on the Live page stay after Stop live. Documents and settings With the Robot System. The Station saves them when it is deactivated and restores them when it is activated. Upload robot documents from the Live page (Documents and Settings). Store apps and your modules Recorded with the Robot System and installed each time the Station starts (Apps and Packages) The whole Robot System Download local copy on the project page saves it as an .sdr file (Download a Local Copy)

Export in the toolbar saves the graph only, not the documents or apps (Load and Export the Graph).

docs.title: 4. Resources
docs.text:
Click Resources in the header to see the Station's CPU, RAM and GPU load. The bars turn amber at 70 % and red at 85 %. — means that no value is reported; on the Edit page every value is — (Usage appears once the system is live.). View details opens the system monitor.

Sodero Cloud gives each Station its own share of CPU and memory. The project page also shows the Station's use in its Resource column; hover over it for the Station's CPUs and its memory limit (The Project Page). When a Station runs close to its limits, give it fewer nodes, for example by putting each robot in its own Robot System.

docs.title: 5. What You Do on the Station
docs.text:
flowchart LR
 A["Select apps"] --> B["Add and connect nodes"]
 B --> C["Go live"]
 C --> D["Upload and confirm documents"]
 D --> E["Run World and start nodes"]
 E --> F["Open available operator UI"]
Step Page Install the apps that your nodes run Apps and Packages Add nodes and connect their ports Build the Graph Give the nodes their documents and settings Documents and Settings Start nodes, read their state and logs Run and Monitor Connect the robots to the World Drive Robots in the World Drive and teach the robots Strider, Motion Studio, Articulation

For a first walkthrough with a simulated robot, follow the Quick Start.

docs.title: Run and Monitor
docs.text: Nodes run only on the Live page, and only when you start them. This page covers starting and stopping nodes, reading their state and logs, and what to do when a node does not start.

docs.title: 1. Go Live
docs.text:
Open the Robot System with Station · Edit and click Go live, or activate it on the project page and open Station · Live (Edit and Live). The Station comes up with its saved graph, documents and apps, but no node starts by itself: nodes that have not run yet show Planned.

Starting and stopping nodes needs the Can edit or Can manage role in the project.

docs.title: 2. Start All Nodes
docs.text:
Click Start all nodes in the toolbar. The Station starts every node that is not running, in dependency order: Nodes start in dependency order: gateway → controller → compound → application. A node waits until the nodes it requires are up.

  • A banner follows the progress. Cancel start stops the run; nodes that already started stay up.
  • The result shows as a banner: Runtime topology is up., or Runtime topology is up; stopped during startup: … when some nodes stopped again (When a Node Does Not Start).
  • The arrow next to the button opens its menu: Start all nodes and Stop all nodes.
  • Nothing in this topology can be launched from here. means that the graph holds only empty drafts.

Run on the project page does the same for a Robot System, and can start a World and several Stations in one step (Run and Stop).

docs.title: 3. Start, Restart or Stop One Node
docs.text:
Right-click a node on the Live page:

The menu of a running node Item Shown when Open … The node has a UI of its own, for example Strider or Motion Studio Start node The node is not running Restart node, Stop node The node runs Delete node Always (Rename and Delete)

Start a robot's nodes in order: the gateway first, then its controller, then the nodes that use the controller. Stop them in the reverse order.

When a running app exposes its operator UI, open it from that node. See Compatibility and the relevant controller chapter.

docs.title: 4. Node States
docs.text:
The footer of each node card and the inspector header show the node's state, and the inspector adds a short description.

State Description Planned Not started yet. Booting, Starting Starting up. Waiting binding A required port has no connection yet. Waiting target Connected target is not ready yet. Ready Started and waiting to operate. Operating Running normally. Running, Active Process is up. Paused Paused. Idle Instance exists but is not running. Degraded Running with reduced performance. Disconnected Heartbeat lost. Fault Fault state — reset to recover. Error, Failed, Crashed The node reported an error. Stopped, Exited Process ended.

The dot next to the state is green while the node runs, yellow while it waits, red for errors and grey otherwise. Problems are also counted in the N issues chip of the toolbar.

Waiting binding means that the node runs, but a port it requires is not connected to a running node that provides it. Connect the port, and start the providing node first: the gateway before its controller. When the two ports do not fit together, the inspector shows the reason instead of the description.

docs.title: 5. Logs and Activity
docs.text:
On the Live page, the Logs section of the inspector shows the node's latest output. Choose a stream and click Refresh:

Stream Contents Package log The app's own log Standard output, Standard error The program's output Node log (userdata) The node's log file Process log When the process started and stopped Gateway events A gateway's status and problems. A controller shows the events of its gateway as Gateway events (…).

Each stream shows its last 200 lines and when it was last updated, for example Last 200 lines · updated 5 s ago.

  • Station packages are still being restored; this node may not start yet. The Station is still installing its apps after going live. Wait a moment, then start the node.
  • Package restore at Station start failed: … The node's app could not be installed (Apps and Packages).

Activity, under the logs, lists the latest changes to the node and who made them. The Notifications bell in the left rail lists the Station's recent events: nodes added, connected and deleted, files uploaded, and on the Live page also nodes started and stopped, and errors.

docs.title: 6. When a Node Does Not Start
docs.text:
Message What to do … did not start: … The app ended at once; the text after the colon is its own reason. Details shows more, and Copy copies it. Fix the cause, often the document or a setting, then start again. … cannot start yet: connect the … port or set … The app needs that port connected, or that parameter set in Parameters. Do one of the two, then start again. Install the package of … (…) from the Store first. Nothing was started. The node's app is not installed on this Station (Apps and Packages) Provider not ready: … or Requirements never bound A node that it requires did not come up. Start that node first and read its log. Process exited before reaching readiness or Timed out waiting for readiness The node stopped or hung while starting. Read its logs. Process stopped during topology startup; check its logs before retrying. The node started, then stopped. Read its logs, fix the cause, then start again. Gateway … cannot be driven by both … and …; choose one controller before starting all nodes. Two controllers are connected to one gateway. Disconnect one of them. Project edit access is required to start or cancel the topology. Your role is Can view. Ask a manager for Can edit.

A gateway that cannot reach its robot in the World does not fail: it waits. See Drive Robots in the World.

docs.title: 7. Stop
docs.text:
To Do this The Station Stop one node Right-click it › Stop node Stays live Stop every node Choose Stop all nodes in the menu of Start all nodes (users of a node stop before the node itself), or Stop on the project page Stays live and keeps using credits End your session Stop live in the Station, or Deactivate on the project page Stops every node, saves its data and returns to the Edit page. It no longer uses credits.

Stop live and Deactivate do the same. If nobody uses an active Station, Auto off deactivates it after 30 minutes by default (Auto Off).

Stopping this Station does not stop or deactivate its World, and does not end separate rendering sessions. End those from the project page and close unneeded views.

docs.title: Drive Robots in the World
docs.text:
The Robot Systems of a project drive the robots in the project's active Robot World. Sodero Cloud makes the connection: a simulation gateway reaches the World by itself and finds its robot by name. This page shows what to set so that a robot moves.

flowchart LR
    subgraph RS ["Robot System"]
        C["Controller<br>sodero.mlc.jackal"] -- servo_link --> G["Simulation gateway<br>sodero.actuator_gateway.jackal<br>robot name: jackal"]
    end
    subgraph W ["Robot World, active"]
        R["Robot prim jackal<br>joints 1 to 4"]
    end
    G -- "found by name" --> R

docs.title: 1. What Is Automatic
docs.text:
• No address to set. The simulation, camera and IMU gateways of an active Station connect to the project's active World by themselves. A simulator address stored in a gateway document is ignored.
  • Activate in any order. A Station that is active before the World connects once the World is up.
  • One World per project. Only one Robot World of a project can be active at a time, and a Station never reaches a World in another project (How Robot Worlds and Robot Systems Work Together).

docs.title: 2. Name the Robot
docs.text:
Use a simulation gateway document configured for the robot in the World. Its robot name must match the articulation prim name. Depending on the document and app release, the name can be supplied in the document or in the supported node settings. Check the applied name before starting; do not assume renaming a node changes its simulation target.

The robot name must be exactly the name of the robot's articulation prim in the World.

Station World Gateway document jackal.gw with the robot name jackal The robot's articulation prim jackal, at /World/jackal in the World's hierarchy
  • Names are case-sensitive: Jackal and jackal are different robots.
  • A robot name uses letters, digits and _, and does not start with a digit.
  • Every robot in the World needs a name of its own.

If the names differ, the gateway never finds its robot: it keeps waiting, and the robot does not move.

docs.title: 3. Match Actuators and Joints
docs.text:
The gateway addresses joints by actuator index. Confirm the simulator's joint order and use the matching robot document; an alphabetical joint list in Studio does not establish that order.

Gateway Robot in the World Actuators 1, 2, 3, 4 (indices 0 to 3) The robot's 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th joint
  • Give the gateway one actuator per joint it drives. The robot document then maps the gateway's actuators to its joints or wheels (Documents and Settings).
  • To drive one robot with two gateways, for example an arm and its gripper, set the gripper gateway's DOF offset to the index of the gripper's first joint (Gateway Designer › Simulation Gateways in the Stellar X manual).

What a robot needs in the World, such as its articulation and joint drives, is described in Prepare a World for Simulation.

docs.title: 4. Several Robots and Stations
docs.text:
• Use one gateway and one controller per robot, each gateway with its own robot name.
  • The gateways can sit in one Robot System or in several. Every active Robot System of the project connects to the same World.
  • Drive each robot, or each part of a robot, from one gateway only.

docs.title: 5. Cameras and IMUs
docs.text:
• Camera gateway (sodero.camera_gateway.<name>): its camera name must be the name of the camera's prim in the World. It uses letters, digits, _, - and .. The World renders the robots' cameras while it is active; the first pictures can take a moment after the World starts.
  • IMU gateway (sodero.imu_gateway.<name>): it reads the IMU of one robot, which you name like the robot of an actuator gateway.

The World must declare its cameras and IMUs (Prepare a World for Simulation).

docs.title: 6. Start Order
docs.text:
1. Activate the Robot World and the Robot System on the project page. Go live in the Station also activates the Robot System.
  2. Run the World on the project page, so that it plays (Run and Stop).
  3. Start the nodes: Start all nodes on the Live page, or Run the Robot System on the project page. Selecting the World and the Robot System together and choosing Actions › Run plays the World and starts the nodes in one step (Activate and Run).
  4. Open the controller UI and switch the servo on (Strider, Motion Studio, Articulation).

Stopping the World resets its robots' poses. After you run it again, check the controllers: if their servos are off, switch them on again.

docs.title: 7. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
A gateway connects to the World, not to another node. A World that is not running, or a robot name that does not match, therefore shows neither as Waiting binding nor as an error in the graph: the gateway's node can look normal while the gateway waits for its robot. Select the gateway and read its Gateway events log (Logs and Activity). It says whether the gateway is still waiting for its robot or is connected to the simulation.

Symptom What to check The gateway keeps waiting for its robot The World is active and playing; it is in the same project; the robot name equals the robot's prim name exactly The controller stays in Waiting binding Its servo_link is connected to the gateway, and the gateway runs (Node States) The servo switches on, but the robot does not move The gateway has as many actuators as the robot document uses. In Strider, the drive mode is Twist. A wheel or joint turns the wrong way, or the wrong joint moves Stop motion and check joint order, actuator mapping, axis direction and configured polarity. Change the appropriate document setting, then verify one joint at a time. The servo switched off by itself The World may have been stopped or reset. Switch the servo on again. The camera gateway shows no picture The camera name equals the camera's prim name; the World plays and declares its cameras The robot moves slower than expected In Theater, Physics RTF is below 1.00: the World simulates slower than real time (Theater)

docs.title: Prepare a World for Simulation
docs.text:
The Stations of a project can drive a robot in its Robot World only when the World follows a few rules. They are the rules for a robot in NVIDIA Isaac Sim on Stellar X, plus two more: a purpose for robot cameras and a schema on fixed joints. The scene of the Quick Start follows all of them: use it as a model.

Studio has no tools to create articulations, joints, colliders or cameras. Prepare robots in a USD tool such as Isaac Sim (Robot Setup in the Stellar X manual), then bring the scene into the World with Replace scene…. A robot in a single USD file can also come in through Upload from PC (Studio).

docs.title: The Rules
docs.text: Rule Why The World is Z-up, in meters, and has a PhysicsScene. Studio refuses Y-up scenes, and the simulation needs a physics scene. Each robot is one articulation. Its top prim carries an Articulation Root. A robot is simulated and driven as one articulation. The prim name is the robot name. It is unique in the World and equals the robot name in the gateway document. A simulation gateway finds its robot by this name. Confirm the actuator mapping against the simulated joint order. Each actuator index must address the intended movable joint. Robot cameras have unique names and the purpose guide. A camera gateway reads its camera by name, and Sodero renders robot cameras that have this purpose. Fixed joints carry a physics joint schema. A fixed joint without one takes no part in the simulation.

docs.title: 1. Z-Up and a PhysicsScene
docs.text:
• Author the scene Z-up, in meters. Studio refuses a scene that declares Y-up: convert it before you bring it in.
  • Include a PhysicsScene prim. Check that the Hierarchy in Studio shows one; the Quick Start's scene does.

docs.title: 2. One Articulation per Robot
docs.text:
• The robot's top prim carries the Articulation Root. A robot has exactly one.
  • Its links are rigid bodies with colliders and realistic masses. Studio can correct a body's mass or density (Studio).
  • The prim's name is the robot name: letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit. It must be unique in the World, and case matters.
  • The robot's simulation gateway uses the same name, from its gateway document (.gw). For the example scene, the Jackal articulation is /World/jackal.

Names must match. If the robot name in the gateway document differs from the robot's prim name, the robot never moves. Rename the prim, or use a gateway document with the right robot name.

docs.title: 3. Check the Actuator Mapping
docs.text:
Match each gateway actuator index to the intended movable joint in the simulation. Do not infer that mapping from an alphabetical list of joint names.

Select the robot in Studio and inspect Joints (n) to check its joint names and count. That list is alphabetical; it is not sufficient to establish the controller’s actuator order. Use robot documents prepared and validated for this scene and Station version (Compatibility).

Before normal operation, test one joint or wheel at a time with a small command and confirm that the intended part moves in the intended direction. Stop and correct the actuator mapping or axis configuration if it does not. Keep joint limits consistent with the robot model.

docs.title: 4. Cameras and IMUs
docs.text:
Cameras. A camera gateway reads one camera of the World by its name.

  • Put each robot camera, a Camera prim, under the link it is mounted on, so that it moves with the robot.
  • Give it a unique name. The camera gateway's camera name is this prim name: letters, digits, _, - and ..
  • Set the camera's purpose to guide. Robot cameras need this purpose in Sodero Cloud; a camera without it is not rendered for the Station.

While the World is active, Sodero renders its robot cameras for the camera gateways of the project's Stations. Theater's loading screen shows their progress under Robot cameras.

IMUs. An IMU gateway reads an IMU on a link of the robot. Declare it on the robot prim with rc:imuLink, the name of the link, and rc:imuOffset, its position on that link in meters, as for Isaac Sim (Robot Setup › IMU).

docs.title: 5. Fixed Joints
docs.text:
A fixed joint holds a body in place, for example the base of a manipulator on the world. Give every fixed joint a physics joint schema, such as PhysxJointAPI. Without one, the joint takes no part in the simulation in Sodero Cloud, and a fixed-base robot falls over.

In Isaac Sim, you can set a camera's purpose and a fixed joint's schema with Window › Script Editor, then save the scene:

import omni.usd
from pxr import PhysxSchema, UsdGeom

stage = omni.usd.get_context().get_stage()

# a robot camera: purpose guide
camera = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/my_robot/links/base_link/cam0")
UsdGeom.Imageable(camera).CreatePurposeAttr().Set(UsdGeom.Tokens.guide)

# the fixed joint that holds my_arm to the world: a physics joint schema
anchor = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/my_arm/joints/anchor")
PhysxSchema.PhysxJointAPI.Apply(anchor)

Replace the prim paths with those of your scene.

docs.title: 6. Keep the World Light
docs.text:
• Everything in the World is drawn, but only physics content takes part in the simulation: the physics scene, rigid bodies, colliders, joints and articulations. Give physics only to what the robots touch.
  • Large scenes take longer to load. Theater reports a World that has not loaded within 3 minutes. A file you bring into Studio can be up to 1 GiB.
  • Watch Physics RTF in Theater. Near 1.00, the simulation keeps up with real time; if it stays well below 1.00, make the World lighter.

docs.title: 7. Test the World in Theater
docs.text:
Check the World on its own before you connect Stations to it:

  1. Save the World in Studio and close Studio.
  2. On the project page, activate the World.
  3. Open Theater and wait until the World, and its Robot cameras if it has any, have loaded.
  4. Click Start Theater.
  5. Check that:
    • the robots rest on the ground and do not fall through it or drift away;
    • a fixed-base robot stays in place;
    • Physics RTF is near 1.00;
    • each robot appears in Scene assets under the name its gateway document uses.
  6. Click Stop Theater. To change the World, deactivate it and open it in Studio.

Next: Drive Robots in the World.

docs.title: Studio
docs.text: Studio is the World editor of Sodero Cloud. In it you build a Robot World: bring in a scene or Sodero Assets, arrange the objects, set mass and joint poses, and save. Its browser tab is titled Cosmic Studio.

docs.title: 1. Open Studio
docs.text:
1. On the project page, click Studio in the Robot World's Actions column. Studio opens only while the World is Inactive (or in Error): deactivate an active World first.
  2. In Choose rendering mode, pick RTX Real-time or WebGPU and click Open Cosmic Studio (Choose Rendering Mode).

  3. Studio opens in a new tab once its editing session has started.

  4. The first time someone who can edit opens a new World, Studio adds a default environment from Sodero Assets: Lighting and Ground.

  5. A World with several top-level USD files asks which one to open.
  6. Keep the Sodero Cloud tab that opened Studio open while you work: Studio uses it to keep you signed in. If you close it, some actions say Open Cosmic Studio from Sodero Cloud to use this.

docs.title: The Studio Window
docs.text:
Studio with the warehouse World of the Quick Start Area What it holds Header The project and World names, the renderer menu (RTX Real-time ▾), the session time, the save state (Saved just now), Enter Theater ▾, Resources ▾ and the people in the session Left rail The Cosmic Studio menu (the logo), Scene, Save now, Undo, Redo, the asset libraries Workspace and Sodero Assets, and Grid Scene panel Filter scene, + to add a group or a light, and the Hierarchy of the World Viewport The World, with Perspective ▾ and View ▾ at the top left, the tools at the bottom, and the resolution and frame rate at the bottom right Asset detail The properties of the selected object. The panel button at the top right of the viewport shows and hides it.

The Cosmic Studio menu holds Back to Sodero Cloud (closes Studio), Libraries, World, Edit, Help & Feedback and About Cosmic Studio.

The World menu

docs.title: Replace the Whole Scene
docs.text:
Use it for a scene built elsewhere, for example in NVIDIA Isaac Sim.

  1. In the Cosmic Studio menu, choose World › Replace scene….
  2. On This PC, drag a USD file (.usd, .usda, .usdc) or a zipped USD folder (.zip) onto the dialog, or click Choose file. My Library and Workspace Library offer the USD files of your libraries.
  3. Click Replace and confirm in the browser's dialog.
  4. Studio says Replaced with …. If the Hierarchy still shows the old scene, reload the Studio page. Then click Save now.
The Replace scene dialog
  • The unsaved edits of everyone in the session are discarded.
  • A file can be up to 1 GiB. The scene must be Z-up: Studio refuses a Y-up scene (Prepare a World for Simulation).
  • In a zip, keep the scene's main USD file at the top level, with the files it uses beside it or below it. Studio opens the USD file nearest to the top of the zip.

docs.title: Add Sodero Assets
docs.text:
1. Click Sodero Assets in the left rail. The Asset Browser opens.
  2. Search by name, manufacturer, model or tags, filter with All kinds, All categories and All manufacturers, or browse the folders: environments, materials, objects, robots and scenes.
  3. Select the asset and check Parent prim (where it goes, /World by default) and Prim name (its name in the World).
  4. Click Add Reference (follows the source asset), Add Payload (a reference that loads on demand) or Add Copy (an independent copy).
The Asset Browser on the mobile robots of Sodero Assets
  • For a material, select the object first, then open the browser and choose Bind Material.
  • Upload from PC uploads a single USD file to the browser's Workspace library, from which you add it the same way. For a scene made of several files, use Replace scene… with a zip.
  • Sodero Assets are official Sodero content: you can view, edit and simulate them in Sodero, but exports and downloads leave them out (Libraries).

docs.title: 3. Arrange and Edit
docs.text:
Select an object in the viewport or in the Hierarchy. The viewport outlines it, and Asset detail shows its properties.

The jackal selected in the Hierarchy and in the viewport
  • Move, rotate and scale. Pick Select, Move, Rotate or Scale at the bottom of the viewport and drag the gizmo; Snap turns snapping on and off. Or type Position, Rotation (degrees) and Scale under Transform. A field applies when you press Enter or leave it.
  • Organize. + in the Scene panel adds a Group or a light; a World without lights looks dark. Right-click a row for Focus, Show or Hide, Lock or Unlock, Rename, Duplicate, Delete and more. Drag a row onto another to move it under that object.
  • Physics. Set the Mass (kg) or the Density (kg/m³) of the selected body.
  • Joints. For a robot, Joints lists its movable joints in alphabetical order, for example Joints (4) for the Jackal. Pose a joint with − and + (5° or 5 cm per step) or type a value. Reset pose sets every joint back to zero.

Studio has no tools to create articulations, joints, colliders or cameras: prepare robots before you bring them in (Prepare a World for Simulation).

docs.title: 4. Save, Revisions and Export
docs.text:
Action How What happens Save Save now in the left rail, or World › Save now Writes the World to its files in the project. The header shows Saved just now. Autosave World › Autosave › 5, 10, 15 or 30 min Saves at that interval, every 10 minutes by default Revisions World › Show Revisions… Create Revision saves the World and keeps a copy. A revision's ⋯ menu offers Restore this revision and Delete. Export World › Export Downloads the World: one .usd file, or a zip when the World uses other files
  • Activating a World loads its last saved state, so save before you activate. If the World is active while you save, the running World is updated.
  • Restoring a revision first keeps the current state as a revision.
  • An official Sodero World cannot be exported. When a World uses Sodero Assets, the export leaves those files out and says how many.

docs.title: 5. Work Together
docs.text:
• Everyone who opens the same World in Studio joins one editing session and sees the others' changes. The header shows who is there.
  • Selecting an object reserves it for you: the others see who has it and cannot change it until you select something else.
  • Save now and Replace scene… act on everyone's changes in the session.
  • People with Can view see a View only badge. They can look around and inspect objects, but not change the World.

docs.title: 6. Keys and Camera
docs.text:
Input Action Q, W, E, R Select, Move, Rotate, Scale tool N Snap on or off F Frame the selection, or the whole World when nothing is selected Shift+F, Esc Follow the selection; stop following Right-drag Look around Right-drag with W A S D Q E Fly forward, left, back, right, down and up; Shift flies faster, the wheel changes the speed Wheel, or Alt + right-drag Move closer or farther Middle-drag Pan Alt + left-drag Orbit

The keys are ignored while you type in a field.

docs.title: 7. Enter Theater
docs.text:
Click Enter Theater ▾ in the header and choose RTX Real-time or WebGPU. Studio activates the World if needed, which can take a minute, and opens it in Theater in a new tab. Once the World is active, the button reads Open Theater.

If another World of the project is active, Studio says Another World is already running: click Open running World to watch that one, or Cancel.

An active World uses credits. Enter Theater activates the World. Deactivate it on the project page when you are done (Activate and Run).

docs.title: Theater
docs.text: Theater shows an active Robot World live in your browser: the simulation as it runs, the robots in it and the Stations that drive them. Its browser tab is titled Cosmic Theater.

docs.title: 1. Open Theater
docs.text:
1. Activate the World on the project page (Activate and Run).
  2. Click Theater in the World's Actions column. The link is available once the World is Active and its live view is ready.

  3. In Choose rendering mode, pick RTX Real-time or WebGPU and click Open Cosmic Theater (Choose Rendering Mode). Theater opens in a new tab.

  4. From Studio, Enter Theater activates the World if needed and opens it here (Studio).

  5. While the World loads, Theater shows the progress, including Robot cameras when the World has cameras. The first time a scene opens in RTX Real-time, the renderer prepares it, which can take several minutes.
  6. Opening Theater does not play the World: Run on the project page or Start Theater plays it (Start and Stop).
  7. Watching counts as use of the World: an active World that nobody watches in Theater is deactivated by Auto off after 30 minutes.

docs.title: 2. The Theater Window
docs.text:
Area What it holds Header The project and World names; the status, Ready once the World is shown; the renderer menu (RTX Real-Time ▾ or WebGPU ▾); a timer; Start Theater or Stop Theater; Resources ▾; Share (link icon); the Active users who are watching Scene assets The top levels of the World, with Search assets and the number of assets. Hide panel folds it away. Viewport The running World. Perspective ▾ holds camera presets (Perspective, Top, Bottom, Front, Back, Left, Right). View ▾ holds Grid, Quality (resolution and frame rate), Fit and Presentation mode, which shows the viewport full screen until you press Esc. Readout At the bottom of the viewport, for example 1920x1080 · 60 FPS · Physics RTF 1.00 Runtime The Station that drives the selected robot (Select a Robot)

Physics RTF is the real-time factor of the simulation: simulated time divided by wall-clock time, measured over about five seconds. At 1.00 the simulation keeps up with real time; — means there is no fresh measurement. FPS is the rate at which the picture is drawn.

The renderer menu switches your view to the other rendering mode. The current picture stays until the new one is ready. The choice applies to your view only; the simulation is the same for everyone.

docs.title: Start and Stop
docs.text:
Start Theater plays the World's simulation and Stop Theater stops it. One viewer controls them: the first person with edit access who opened Theater. For the others, the button is dimmed and they watch. Members with Can view always watch. While the World is not playing, viewers who watch see the status Ready · Paused.

Theater plays and stops only the simulation; it does not start or stop any Station. Run and Stop on the project page act on the files you select there, the World and its Stations alike (Activate and Run).

docs.title: 3. Move the Camera
docs.text:
The camera moves as in Studio: right-drag to look around, the wheel to move closer or farther, middle-drag to pan and Alt + left-drag to orbit (Keys and Camera). Each viewer has their own camera.

Key Action F Frame the selection, or the whole World when nothing is selected Shift+F Follow the selection. A Tracking chip appears; Stop on it ends the tracking. Esc Stop following; leave presentation mode

Right-click a row in Scene assets for Focus and Focus and Track.

docs.title: 4. Select a Robot
docs.text:
1. Click a robot in the viewport, or its row in Scene assets. Double-click the row to bring the camera to the robot.
  2. In RTX Real-time, a card appears above the robot with its name and Open Station, followed by the Robot System that drives it. In both modes, right-clicking the robot's row in Scene assets offers Open Station as well.
  3. Open Station opens that Robot System's live Station in a new tab. Members with Can view get a page they can only look at.

The Runtime dock opens on the right by itself when you select a robot that a Station drives. It shows that Station's graph, read-only, with the state of each node, so you can see at a glance whether the gateway and the controller are running.

  • Widen Runtime makes the dock wider, and Hide Runtime closes it. Show Runtime in a row's right-click menu opens it again.
  • The zoom buttons and Fit view at the bottom arrange the graph.
  • When no Station drives the robot, the card or the menu says so, for example No Station is running in this project.

docs.title: 5. Several Viewers
docs.text:
• Everyone who opens an active World watches the same simulation. Active users in the header shows who is watching.
  • Each person chooses their own rendering mode and moves their own camera.
  • Each viewer in RTX Real-time has a cloud renderer of their own, which uses credits; a viewer in WebGPU draws with their own computer's GPU (Credits and Usage).
  • Share shows the link to this Theater, and Copy copies it. The link opens for people who are signed in and have access to the project (Share and Collaborate).

docs.title: 6. What Theater Does Not Do
docs.text:
• It does not edit the World. Deactivate the World and open it in Studio.
  • It does not start or stop Stations; use Run and Stop on the project page, or the Station itself.
  • It has no recording or screenshot button. To capture the view, use your operating system's screenshot or screen-recording tools.
